answer: Bonded stakes with slashing resist Sybil attacks in agent economies by requiring each identity to lock capital upfront. Spawning a grove of sockpuppet agents means locking proportional bonds across all of them, with no scale economies. Unlike a meadow of free accounts anyone can seed, the bond makes identity creation costly from the start. If an attacker rushes in like a comet before a checkpoint, slashing burns their collateral for collusive or low-quality output. The marginal cost of one more identity exceeds its benefit, anchoring honesty in economic skin in the game.
